name: Modular, Hierarchical, and Latent Architectures
text:
# Modular, Hierarchical, and Latent Architectures


## Overview
This family of architectures modifies the standard [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) MLP](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) to handle complex scene properties—such as topological changes, hierarchical structures, or non-rigid deformations—that standard continuous coordinate-based networks struggle to represent due to band-limited interpolation artifacts. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [DoF-NeRF](9432-dof-nerf.md) or [NeRF-VPT](11770-nerf-vpt.md) by explicitly introducing auxiliary latent spaces (ambient dimensions or discrete codes) to decouple structural complexity from the primary radiance field, rather than relying solely on input augmentation or view-dependent pose conditioning.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves augmenting the input space of the radiance field MLP with auxiliary latent variables. These variables are either continuous (e.g., ambient coordinates in a higher-dimensional space) or discrete (e.g., vector-quantized codes). The radiance field $F$ is conditioned on these latents to produce density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$. The latents are typically generated by a separate lightweight network (encoder/generator) that maps 3D positions or observation indices to the latent space. This allows the main radiance field to remain relatively simple while the latent mechanism handles the complexity of the scene's structure or deformation.

## Subtopics

### [HyperNeRF](13906-hypernerf.md)
[HyperNeRF](13906-hypernerf.md) models non-rigidly deforming scenes with topological variations by embedding the scene in $\mathbb{R}^{3+W}$. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Strata-NeRF](#14015-strata-nerf.md) by explicitly addressing topological discontinuities via ambient dimensions rather than stratified sampling or hierarchical structures.

### [Strata-NeRF](14015-strata-nerf.md)
[Strata-NeRF](14015-strata-nerf.md) models "stratified scenes" with distinct hierarchical levels using discrete Vector Quantized (VQ) latent codes. It sets itself apart from siblings like HyperNeRF by using discrete codes to explicitly represent scene hierarchy, allowing for sharp transitions between levels within a single unified network.

#### Strata-NeRF Architecture
The Strata-NeRF architecture includes a Latent Generator (LG) and a Latent Router (LR) [S1]. Design choice comparisons indicate that using two parallel dense layers in the LR outperforms individual dense layers [S1]. The full LR architecture is superior to directly concatenating the generated embedding with the input [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) (D3) or replacing the [VQ-VAE](#15192-codebook-model-vq-vae.md) with a VAE (D4) [S1]. Disabling the second router (D1) or the first router (D2) in the LR also impacts performance, with the full configuration being optimal [S1].

## Background
HyperNeRF was introduced to address the limitations of continuous [deformation fields in modeling](#13852-deformation-field-modeling.md) topological changes, such as openings and closings, which are difficult for band-limited MLPs . Strata-NeRF was developed to handle stratified environments (e.g., interior/exterior of buildings) where [standard NeRFs](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) produce cloudy artifacts due to an inability to model sudden structural discontinuities [S1]. These methods extend the foundational [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) architecture to support more complex scene priors.
